Optional mixed native leaves
============================

Ordinary Cesta builds use readable C and the selected C compiler. They require
neither tcalc nor HOL Light. This adapter is a separate experiment for selected
scalar leaves; it does not replace the ordinary compiler route.

  make build/cesta-tisa
  build/cesta-tisa build/cesta SOURCE FUNCTION SYMBOL OUTPUT.S OUTPUT.json

The adapter first checks the source through Cesta, then lowers the selected
function directly into tcalc's existing TcIsaProgram and byte emitter. It accepts
the unsigned-select/1 profile: bool, u32, u64 and 64-bit usize parameters/results,
unsigned comparisons, scalar literals, and a return or pure returning conditional.
It admits at most five parameters and refuses expressions beyond its register
capacity. Pointer operations, allocation, loops and calls remain outside this
initial profile. Other Cesta and standard C code retain the ordinary C route.

The emitted function uses the existing t-ISA runtime-frame argument followed by
its scalar arguments. Its scalar result is available in RAX and frame.ret_val;
frame.status distinguishes success from exhaustion. Boolean and u32 inputs must
be canonical values of their declared types. The target is x86-64 SysV LP64.
The current execution policy retains fuel accounting, including budget zero.
The function body has no spills; its ABI prologue still saves registers on the
stack. Static target objects contain no executable-memory loader.

The examples connect a selected prefix-length function to the existing u32 span
copy module. MixedKernel.cesta supplies the ordinary-C two-call wrapper;
MixedCopy.cesta is an independently checked caller with explicit bounds guards,
slices and imported copy. The host owns each count call's frame.

  make qualify-mixed-leaves
  make qualify-hol-mixed-leaves

MIXED_LEAF_FLAGS may pass --out, --tcalc, --s2n and --hol. The proof target needs
external HOL Light and s2n-bignum checkouts. Qualification checks both GCC and
Clang, source admission, scalar controls, paired copies, fuel outcomes,
sanitizers, instruction identity, semantic mutations and exact ELF identities.
It also rebuilds the exported C and assembly from a relocated directory without
Cesta, HOL or the t-ISA emitter. SHA256SUMS is a flat list of the exported inputs;
existing dependency licences accompany copied declarations.

The runtime consumes a static copy of the complete linked text image. Symbols
for the count, copy and wrapper select their original extents inside that image,
so internal calls retain their exact relative instruction bytes. The proof
derives decode rules from each actual function; unreachable linker padding has
no execution rule. A proof cannot step into such a gap.

PREFIX_COUNT_CORRECT proves the selected count artifact's result and frame
writes with budget zero. COPY_GCC_CORRECT and COPY_CLANG_CORRECT prove their
selected copy artifacts. MIXED_GCC_CORRECT and MIXED_CLANG_CORRECT compose the
actual calls, including their stack and ABI return. Under valid, aligned,
nonoverlapping ranges and the declared stack/frame conditions, the result is
min(source.len,destination.len), that prefix is copied, and unrelated memory is
preserved. Counts are elements; source/destination memory extents use four bytes
per element. The copied input and destination capacities are below 2^61.

The native copy's declared failure edge remains outside its admitted input
contract. Nonzero fuel budgets have separate runtime controls; the first mixed
machine theorems cover budget zero. Kernel privilege, interrupts, device memory
and concurrent callers require their own execution contracts.

The optional proof gate requires both complete caller theorems, a fresh process,
an axiom audit and refusal of a semantically changed count instruction. A receipt
with proof_status not-run is runtime evidence. Source lowering and the Cesta
frontend remain tested boundaries; the selected artifact theorems do not prove
the general emitter or general C execution. Changing compiler flags, headers,
source or target requires qualification against the resulting artifacts.

The benchmark compares the same compiled copy leaf with an ordinary C count and
with the explicit t-ISA frame/count path. It reports repeated complete-call
observations on the current host. It makes no general performance claim and
does not change the default backend.
